Kenosha Public Market is a year-round Saturday market located in the heart of the Downtown district. Our vendors present a variety of products including local produce, artisan pastries and confections, locally sourced meats, poultry and eggs, fine cheeses, prepared foods & handmade gifts. organization.description:
The GSFM is unique collaboration between local organizations with a shared goal of creating conditions under which people can be healthy. It is one of few markets in downtown Louisville and is dedicated to increasing availability of fresh foods to an underserved area. The market offers customers a great variety of local vendors and products. We are open the first Thursday of each month from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. from June through October.

HISTORY: In 2009, the University of Louisville School of Public Health and Information Sciences (SPHIS) led efforts to establish the Gray Street Farmers Market (GSFM) in partnership with the Louisville Metro Dept. of Public Health and Wellness (LMPHW). The GSFM operated weekly (rain or shine) from mid-May through the end of October for 11 seasons. We did not open in 2019 or 2020 due to COVID-19 pandemic and resource limitations .

organization.description: With a focus on Michigan grown and Michigan made foods, the Battle Creek Farmers Market is a great place to find fresh and flavor packed local foods from Michigan businesses. Non-food businesses are also welcome. The Market is held in Festival Market Square in downtown Battle Creek on Wednesday, 9-1, beginning in May and ending in October. Customers will find a family friendly market with a good variety of variety of vendors. Vendors will find a well managed and vendor friendly market. An open air marketplace under a pavilion offers picnic tables, restrooms onsite and free 1-hour parking for customers in the Hamblin Avenue ramp. Live music and other activities make summer fun at the farmers market. BCFM participates in Bridge Card (SNAP), Double Up Food Bucks, Senior Market FRESH, WIC Project FRESH, NHBP Elders Nutrition Program. Payment with cash, Credit and Debit cards as well a market issued scrip accepted. Contact us for more information. Visit us on Facebook and Instagram, too!

organization.description: The Running Springs Area Chamber of Commerce Certified Farmers Market and Artisan Faire runs every Saturday, April 25 - November 21 (the Saturday before Thanksgiving), 9am-1pm. Enjoy a wide variety of Vegetables & Fruit, Herbs, Cage-Free Eggs, Fresh Bread, Jam, Coffee, Mexican Food, Food Artisans, Sweets, Art, Products, Clothing, Body Products, Jewelry, Nonprofit information, and Live Music. Updates are posted on Facebook & Twitter @RSfarmersmarket or Instagram @RS_farmersmarket. The market is nestled between a very nice playground, picnic tables, and the Running Springs Branch Library at 2645 Whispering Pines Drive. At 6,000 feet elevation, the field has nice views of nearby pine trees, blue skies (mostly) and cooler mountain temperatures. The area is considered a Gateway to the San Bernardino Mountains. Many visitors come year-round to enjoy the San Bernardino National Forest.

organization.description:
The largest weekly, year-round farmers market in the county, voted “Best of Westchester” in 2014 - 2025, twelve years in a row! With over 60 vendors, 9 nearby parking lots, live music, culinary demos, kids events, and nutritional talks, the Market is located in Memorial Plaza, in the heart of the historic Village of Pleasantville. Please note the Market is a dog-free environment.
SNAP benefits are doubled (up to $40) at Pleasantville Farmers Market. Redeem $40 in benefits, get $80 to spend, thanks to a generous grant from our local hospitals, Phelps Hospital and Northern Westchester Hospital, both part of the Market’s Lead Sponsor Northwell Health. WIC & Seniors Farmers Market Nutrition Program checks can also be used to purchase fruit and vegetables at the Market. Stop by the Managers Tent for assistance.

organization.description:
Brookside Farmers’ Market is an sustainable, regenerative, pesticide-free local, producer-only market. Producers use organic, sustainable and cruelty-free practices, travel less than 125 miles to market, and those who grow, raise or make every product are the ones who sell it to you directly.

Each Saturday you will find just-picked, farm-fresh vegetables and herbs, bright flowers, delicious meats, eggs from free-range chickens, freshly prepared breads and baked goods including many vegan and gluten-free items, fresh juices, and a place to sit and take in the scene.

The market has brought farm fresh produce to the Brookside neighborhood and beyond since 2003.

The market is located at HJ’s Community Center and is open Saturdays 8 a.m. to 1 p.m. through October 31. Check website for WINTER MARKET dates, hours, and location.

organization.description:
Cuyahoga Valley Farmers Markets’ (CVFM) works to provide access to and education about sustainable foods and agriculture to the communities in Northeast Ohio by building connections between our community with the producers of locally grown food.
CVFM was established in 2022 to continue the operation of the long-running Countryside farmers markets in Howe Meadow and at Old Trail School, both located in the Cuyahoga Valley National Park. These vibrant farmers markets have been in operation since 2004 and have been growing steadily since their inception.
CVFM MARKET IMPACT:
During our Summer market in Howe Meadow (May-October) we connect on average 2,500 (peak 3,000) members of our community to producers of local food.
During our Winter market at Old Trail School (November-April) we have on average 600 shoppers per market (peak 1,000).
Provide consistent sales outlet for 70 local farms and businesses.

organization.description: Common Ground Producers and Growers is a mobile farmers market and food hub. It is a family-run agricultural organization based in Wichita, Kansas, operating the state’s longest-running Mobile farmers market and food hub. Founded in 2014 by multi-generational farmer and CEO Donna Pearson McClish, the organization was established to eliminate food insecurity by delivering fresh, locally grown produce directly into neighborhoods with limited access to healthy food. Guided by the motto “All are fed. No one is hungry.” Common Ground operates on Pearson’s Family Farms—the largest Black-owned urban farm in the region. On the farm, Common Ground aggregates, processes, and distributes Kansas-grown fruits and vegetables sourced from more than 40 farmers statewide. The mobile farmers market and food hub currently serves 37 locations across 10 cities and 4 counties, while ensuring equitable compensation for farmers and maintaining affordable prices for customers.

name: The TaSh (the Tarrytown Sleepy Hollow) Farmers Market

location.description:
Located at Patriots Park, in Tarrytown NY during our Summer Market.
Winter Market is located indoors at John Paulding School, across the street from the park.

organization.description:
The Tarrytown and Sleepy Hollow Farmers Market – The TaSH – is a destination in Westchester County. Farm-fresh fruits and vegetables, artisanal breads and baked goods, meats, poultry, fish, craft spirits, farmhouse cheeses – it’s all here.

The TaSH is set in historic Patriots Park on NY State Route 9, straddling the scenic Hudson River villages of Tarrytown and Sleepy Hollow. Each Saturday, May through November, 50+ vendor stalls hug a sun-dappled, grassy lawn, where the best area musicians entertain. Kids dance and play, friends and families socialize, and everyone eats!

We host chef demos, art projects, children’s activities and we welcome our fellow non-profit organizations to share their good works too.

We make the market accessible to everyone through food access programs, shopper rewards and bilingual translation.

location.description: Brunswick, Maine, located in the Fort Andross Mill on the Androscoggin River.

organization.description: We created the first winter market in Maine and are located in Fort Andross, an old mill along the Androscoggin River. Our vendors live in Maine and represent their own business. We are farmers, bakers, product producers, craftspersons enthusiastically supported by the community. Our partnership the Maine Federation of Farmer’s Markets, we accept SNAP payments and offer the Bonus Bucks program, which gives SNAP customers extra 'money’ to spend on food purchased at our market. Most proudly, we are a vendor-run market, a co-operative entity, with major decision making decided by the market vendor/members. We hold an annual meeting to address any changes and concerns as well as a New Vendor Meeting where all vendor hopefuls can meet the membership and present their business with the hope of filling any vacant positions for the coming market season.

location.description: Shelburne Parade Grounds, Shelburne, VT. At the corner of Shelburne Rd and Church Street.

organization.description:
We’re a producer-only farmers market on the Shelburne, VT, Parade Grounds, meeting every Saturday, mid-May through mid-October. The market is where local farms and makers welcome their neighbors and visitors to the best of Shelburne. It’s a Third Space — not home, not work — where the community shows up for each other once a week. We welcome vendors of all backgrounds — including New Americans and neighbors who haven’t sold here before.

Our Mission:
1. Create true community wealth
2. Strengthen Shelburne’s quality of life
3. Close the gaps in the food system
4. Steward a sustainable, enduring market

Impact Indicators
1. Community access
2. Service
3. Farmer value and participation
4. Business incubation
5. Stewardship

location.description: Forked Deer River Park - Downtown Dyersburg

organization.description:
We love our amazing community for supporting our producer only farmers market in downtown Dyersburg! We’re so thrilled to be located in the heart of downtown within the beautiful Forked Deer River park, and we’re even more excited to offer live music, activities, story time, food trucks, dancing, and so much more to complement our fantastic market vendors!
Opening day is always the 2nd Saturday in June and we’ll be open from 8am to noon every Saturday through September. So come on down, play at the splash pad, check out the park, and support our market! We can’t wait to see you there! The Main Street Dyersburg Farmers Market runs June–September, and as a producer-only market, every item you see here is either handmade or locally grown.
